edges.effect_quant: In the Melbourne cohort, 28.4% of male C282Y homozygotes and 1.2% of female homozygotes had documented iron-overload-related disease, while a Copenhagen hereditary hemochromatosis cohort found ferritin above 1000 ug/L in 39.0% of homozygous patients versus 14.5% of compound heterozygotes.
edges.population: people with HFE hereditary hemochromatosis, especially C282Y homozygotes
edges.mechanism: HFE mutations reduce hepcidin signaling and increase intestinal iron absorption, causing progressive transferrin saturation and ferritin elevation over time. Once the iron-buffering capacity is exceeded, excess iron accumulates in the liver, joints, pancreas, heart, and other tissues.
edges.summary: Hereditary hemochromatosis is one of the clearest genetic drivers of systemic iron overload, especially in C282Y homozygotes. Population and clinic cohorts consistently show elevated ferritin and transferrin saturation in carriers with clinically important overload concentrated in a substantial minority of men and a smaller but real fraction of women.
edges.caveats: Penetrance is incomplete, so not every genetically affected person develops overt organ injury, particularly in population-screened cohorts and in women before menopause. Even so, the relationship to biochemical iron loading is strong enough that the edge itself is not meaningfully in doubt.
